summary: @servicetitan/assist-utils 1.1.8 ships preinstall Bun-runtime dropper executing obfuscated payload
details: The package declares `scripts.preinstall = "node setup.mjs"`, which fires automatically on `npm install`. `setup.mjs` is heavily obfuscated (obfuscator.io-style `_0xNNNN` identifiers with string-dictionary indirection) and downloads the Bun runtime (bun-v1.3.13) from `github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases`, extracts the `bun` binary into a temp directory, chmods it executable, and invokes it via `execFileSync(bunPath, [<path to math_init.js>])` against the package-local `math_init.js` — a 727 KB Bun-format payload with rotating string-array obfuscation (`WV8StW` shift/rotate, mangled identifiers, opaque char-code table). The package presents itself as a React/MobX host-MFE utility library (`main:./dist/index.js`, CHANGELOG referencing servicetitan/ti-assist-fe), a purpose entirely inconsistent with pulling an alternate language runtime at install time to execute an obfuscated sibling bundle. The Bun runtime is used specifically to run code that is not Node-resolvable, evading scanners that only inspect JavaScript reachable from `main`. The pattern is the canonical alternate-runtime-dropper: legitimate runtime fetched from its official source, then used to execute attacker-controlled obfuscated bytes bundled with the package. Combined with the obfuscation of the preinstall script itself and the mismatch with the package's advertised purpose, this indicates either compromise of the @servicetitan publishing credentials or a scope-hijack publish.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
